stem: In the figure, \(\overline{PA}\) and \(\overline{PB}\) are tangent to the circle with center \(O\) at points \(A\) and \(B\), respectively. The measure of angle \(APB\) is \(50^{\circ}\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(AOB\)?
solution: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, so angles \(OAP\) and \(OBP\) each measure \(90^{\circ}\).
The angles of quadrilateral \(OAPB\) add to \(360^{\circ}\): \(m\angle AOB = 360 - 90 - 90 - 50 = 130\).
verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert abs(ang('O','A','P')-90)<0.1 and abs(ang('O','B','P')-90)<0.1 and abs(ang('A','P','B')-50)<0.1
ans=360-90-90-50
assert abs(ang('A','O','B')-ans)<0.1
assert all(Rational(s)==ans==130 for s in spr_answers)
